Commentary.Commentary: We are back. Will O'Rourke to bowl first. Mohammad Haris and Hasan Nawaz to open for Pakistan. A slip in place. Let's play...
...THE CHASE...

Pakistan once again have a mountain to climb! All eyes will be on Hasan Nawaz! The centurion has to help his team once again and so should the other batters if they want to keep the series alive. New Zealand have changed their bowling attack. The start will set the tone for the rest of the innings. An interesting chase coming up. Stay tuned.

Pakistan once again bowled similarly to the way we have seen in this series. Pakistan's bowling was woefully ineffective early on but improved significantly in the middle overs. However, New Zealand finished with a flourish, as skipper Michael Bracewell played a masterful hand to propel his team beyond 200 in the final 4 overs. Haris Rauf was Pakistan's standout bowler, claiming three wickets, while Abrar Ahmed secured two, albeit at a costly expense. Salman Agha shuffled his bowlers regularly. He used Haris Rauf particularly really well, however, didn't get much support from others.

New Zealand's innings unfolded in three distinct phases, ultimately culminating in a formidable total. The hosts seized control in the first 10 overs, with Tim Seifert setting the tone with a blistering 44 off 20 deliveries. Finn Allen initially played a supporting role but soon accelerated, surpassing Tim Seifert's strike rate and reaching a half-century before departing. Once he fell, the Kiwis nosedived a bit and lost control of the match. However, the partnership between Daryl Mitchell and Michael Bracewell blossomed and helped New Zealand get to the 220 mark.

Michael Bracewell said at the toss that they missed out on a crucial partnership after a good start in the last match. Well, they were under similar circumstances today as well but have got that extra cushion of runs right at the fag end of the innings. However, is it enough or New Zealand have left some runs out there in the middle is the question? Time will tell.

Commentary.Commentary: A halt in play as the Pakistani players are quickly hydrating themselves. Change in bowling, Abrar Ahmed is into the attack.
Slower short delivery on middle, Seifert pulls it to deep square leg for a single. 15 runs off the over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Shaheen Afridi to Tim Seifert, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Big over already! Bowls it in the slot, Seifert pre-meditates, gets in the shape as he rocks back and smashes it over long off for a huge six.

Commentary.Commentary: Change of pace from Afridi! At 119 clicks! On a length and on top of off. Seifert taps it to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Shaheen Afridi to Tim Seifert, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A good length delivery on middle, Allen knocks it in front of mid on and takes a sharp single.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Freebie! Looks for the swing but dishes out a full toss on the pads. Allen whips it over mid-wicket and it rolls to the fence.

Commentary.Commentary: THREE RUNS! Pitched up swinging on middle, Seifert flicks it through mid-wicket. The fielder gives the chase and slides near the fence to save a run for his team. Abbas Afridi it was.

Commentary.Commentary: Floats it a bit, full and on middle, Seifert skips down and lofts off the inner half of the bat and to long on for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up full and on middle, arm delivery and Seifert punches it to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Khushdil Shah to Tim Seifert, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: TWO WIDES! 11 already of the over! Down the leg side again, Allen fails to hit it away and it rolls to fine leg for a single. Easy runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Khushdil Shah to Finn Allen, 2 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: TWO WIDES! Spills it full and down the leg side, Seifert fails to sweep and it rolls to short fine leg of the keeper's leg for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Not the length you would like to bowl on this pitch! Short once again from Shah, outside off and Seifert punches it to cover.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Pure strength from Seifert! Fractionally short from Shah and Seifert quickly moves on the back foot, he opens up his body and thumps it down the ground for a biggie.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter delivery, outside off, Seifert slaps it straight to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Khushdil Shah to Tim Seifert, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slightly short and on middle, Allen pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single. He is off the mark.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl now? It is Khushdil Shah!
FOUR! Streaky! Afridi targets the stumps again, goes full and on middle, swinging in late. Seifert looks to cut but bottom edges it past the stumps and to fine leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Shaheen Afridi to Tim Seifert, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! Quality from Afridi! Shaheen Afridi drags his length back and bowls it outside off, shaping in late. Seifert looks to punch it but misses.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Shaheen Afridi to Tim Seifert, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: How has that missed the stumps? Wow! Superb from Afridi! Touch fuller and swinging in around off. Seifert is late to get his bat down and gets beaten on the outside edge. It goes past the off pole as well. Even Shaheen Afridi looks surprise as it misses the stumps.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Shaheen Afridi to Tim Seifert, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Shot from a man who is full of confidence! Shaheen Afridi pitches it up and bowls it on middle, Seifert with a straight bat drives it down past mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Shaheen Afridi to Tim Seifert, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Not on the money but quality delivery from Afridi! A yorker, shaping on the pads and swinging away a bit. Seifert looks to flick it but misses and gets hit on the boots.

Commentary.Commentary: All set for action. A quick word by Salman Agha to his team before they spread out in the middle. The explosive openers of Kiwis, Tim Seifert and Finn Allen walk to the middle. The Eagle from Pakistan, Shaheen Afridi takes the new ball as he always does. A slip in place. Let's go...
Time for the national anthems! Both teams stride out to the middle. It will be of Pakistan's team first followed by the Kiwis.

Michael Bracewell, the captain of New Zealand says Eden Park is a special ground and strange things have happened there. Tells that they needed one more partnership in the last match to push the score around 230-240 runs which could have been enough to defend the score down. Mentions Bay Oval is a completely different ground, they need to assess the conditions quickly and set a target they will be confident defending.
Salman Agha, the skipper of Pakistan says they will bowl first, it worked for them in the last match and want to replicate. Adds they are a good enough team to play under any conditions.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tim Seifert, Finn Allen, Mark Chapman, Daryl Mitchell, James Neesham, Mitchell Hay (WK), Michael Bracewell (C), Zakary Foulkes (In for Kyle Jamieson), Ish Sodhi, Jacob Duffy, Will O'Rourke (In for Ben Sears).
Pakistan (Unchanged Playing XI) - Mohammad Haris (WK), Hasan Nawaz, Salman Agha (C), Irfan Khan, Shadab Khan, Abdul Samad, Khushdil Shah, Abbas Afridi, Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf, Abrar Ahmed.
TOSS - Pakistan have won the toss and will BOWL first!

New Zealand didn’t do much wrong. A score more than 200 should have been defended down but their bowlers for the first time in this series looked a bit tired. They know it was just a bad day at the office and would be eager to bounce back and seal the series today itself. Also, Matt Henry was ruled out for the first three matches but now will miss the remainder of the series as well, as he is recovering from a shoulder injury. Will the hosts take the inevitable lead or Pakistan with a lot of confidence now, come back from behind and take the series into the final game? We shall find out soon. Toss and team news coming up in a bit.

Hello and welcome to the fourth T20I between New Zealand and Pakistan. This series has come alive with a comprehensive win from the tourists. After two consecutive ducks, Hasan Nawaz scored a magnificent century and helped his team chase down over 200 in just 16 overs. Mohammad Haris and Salman Agha played a solid helping hand to keep the series alive. Pakistani batters have finally come to the party and kept the series alive, they now have to replicate what they did in the last match. However, the Pakistani bowlers, consisting of Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf and Abrar Ahmed have performed not to their potential but still two games to go, they would hope to produce a better performance.
...MATCH DAY...

The Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui is all set to host the 4th T20I between hosts New Zealand and Pakistan as we near the conclusion of the five-match series. The Kiwis seemed well in control with a couple of very comfortable wins in the first two games and then riding on a superb 94 off just 44 balls from Mark Chapman, New Zealand notched up 200-plus runs in the 3rd T20I in Auckland. However, a storm by the name of Hasan Nawaz came and blew everything away as he scored a sensational ton and somehow, Pakistan managed to knock over the target in just 16 overs, keeping the series well and truly alive. The fourth T20I will be a crucial game for both sides as a win for the Kiwis would seal the series for them but a win for Pakistan would mean that the fifth and final T20I would become a straight shootout for the series victory. New Zealand have made a few changes to their squad for the final two T20I games and the left-arm spinner, Nikith Perera has been named in the squad and we might even see him get a senior international debut soon. On the other hand, Pakistan has the same squad, but we might now see more of a settled XI with the batting starting to take shape. Hasan Nawaz and Mohammad Haris up top make for a brute pair up top and the skipper, Salman Agha is that glue coming in at number 3. The bowling leaves a lot to be desired from the visitors as the experienced likes of Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf and Shadab Khan haven't quite lived up to expectations. Also, the batting can collapse at any given moment as we have seen so many times in the past but the previous game should give them a lot of confidence. New Zealand on the other hand does have a somewhat inexperienced bowling lineup and even the batting doesn't have the regular names but barring the previous game, they have shown great application on both fronts and will be looking to get back to winning ways after that unprecedented way of defeat. Will they be able to do so? Or will Pakistan keep building momentum and level things up? Only time will tell.
